AddBatchItemRequest.description: Request model for adding an item to a batch.

itemID.description:
The ID of the **existing** item to add to the batch.
For Content Items: use the ContentID of an existing content item
For Page Items: use the PageID of an existing page
This must be a valid, existing item ID in your CMS.

itemTitle.description:
Optional display title for the item in the batch for identification purposes.
If not provided, the system will fetch and use the actual title from the existing item.
This is just for display - it doesn't change the actual content.

languageCode.description: The language code for the item (e.g., "en-us", "fr-ca", "es-mx").

AllTypesResponse.description:
Response model containing all enum types used throughout the Management API.
This provides a single source of truth for all enum metadata.

batchItemTypes.description: Available batch item types (page, content item, etc.).

batchOperationTypes.description: Available batch operation types (publish, approve, etc.).

changeItemTypes.description: Available change item types for tracking.

contentModelTypes.description: Available content model types (item, list, module).

contentViewTypes.description: Available content view types (all, shared, linked, etc.).

itemStates.description: Available item states (new, staging, published, etc.).

pageItemTemplateTypes.description: Available page item template types (variable, fixed module).

workflowOperationTypes.description: Available workflow operation types (subset of batch operations).

BatchCreateResult.description:
The outcome of queueing work that may not fit in one batch.
            
An item list longer than Agility.Management.Domain.Models.Batch.MaxItemsPerBatch is split across several batches
rather than rejected, the same way {ImportUrlRedirections} chunks a large import instead
of failing it. Every batch that was created is named here, so a caller can poll all of them
rather than watching one finish while the rest are still running.

batchCount.description:
How many batches the work was split across — {BatchIDs.Count}, named so clients do
not have to infer it.

batchIDs.description: The batches that were queued, in the order the items were submitted. Usually one.

failedItemCount.description:
Items that were not queued because the batch carrying them failed to create. Normally zero.
            
A partial failure still returns the batches that did queue — discarding them would leave the
caller unable to poll work that is already running - so the shortfall is reported here
rather than thrown, and logged as an error. A total failure throws instead: there is nothing
to poll, and a 200 there would be exactly the silent success these counts exist to prevent.

itemCount.description:
Total items actually queued across every batch.
            
This counts batch rows, not the content those rows resolve to at processing time: a
{ContentList} row is one item here and publishes its whole container.
            
It counts what was queued, never what was submitted. If a batch failed to create, its items
are counted in Agility.Management.Domain.Models.BatchCreateResult.FailedItemCount instead, so the two always add back up to the
list the caller sent and this number cannot overstate the work in flight.

BatchItemType.description: Types of items that can be added to a batch.

BatchOperationType.description: All batch operation types - includes workflow operations and other batch operations.

BatchState.description: States that a batch can be in during its lifecycle.

CascadeItem.description:
A node in a cascade tree — the parent item plus the nested items a cascading publish would
bring with it. Port of the shape Classic's {Batch/GetCascadeItemsForPage} returned to the
Advanced Selection dialog, minus its knockout-specific display flags.
            
This is discovery only: the caller picks the nodes it wants and submits them to
{POST batch}. Nothing here enqueues anything.

children.description: Nested items one level below this node.

expanded.description: Whether a tree UI should render this node expanded by default.

itemID.description: The item's ID — an itemContainerID for pages and content items, a contentViewID for lists.

key.description:
Stable per-node key — {p-{id}} for a page, {ci-{id}} for a content item,
{cv-{id}} for a content list. Matches the keys Classic emitted so a client can
treat the two responses interchangeably.

languageCode.description: Locale the node was resolved in.

CreateBatchWithItemsRequest.description:
Request model for creating a batch and its items in one call.
            
This is the Management API's replacement for Classic's {Batch/Update}, the only route
that accepted an arbitrary {Items[]}. It is what the Advanced Selection flow needs:
read a tree from a {cascade-items} endpoint, let the user prune it, submit what is left.

batchName.description: Custom name for the batch. If not provided, defaults to "Custom Batch".
batchName.example: Publish landing page and its modules

comments.description: Optional comments or notes about the batch, stored as the batch's additional data.
comments.example: Cascade selected in the publish dialog

isPrivate.description: Whether the batch should be private (visible only to the creator). Defaults to true.

items.description:
The items the batch should act on. Must contain at least one item; a list longer than
Agility.Management.Domain.Models.Batch.MaxItemsPerBatch is split across several batches rather than rejected.

UrlRedirection.description:
A URL redirection rule. Saving an item without a Agility.Management.Domain.Models.UrlRedirection.UrlRedirectionID creates a new
redirection; a positive ID updates (fully replaces) the existing redirection.

content.description: Optional content served for the redirect instead of a Location header.

destinationLocale.description: Optional locale code (e.g. "en-us") of the destination URL.

destinationUrl.description: The URL (or path) to redirect to.

httpCode.description: The HTTP status code for the redirect: 301 (permanent) or 302 (temporary).

originLocales.description: Optional locale codes the origin URL applies to. Empty or null applies to all locales.

originUrl.description: The incoming URL (or path) to redirect from. Must be unique within the instance.

UrlRedirectionDeleteResult.description: Outcome of a multi-item URL redirection delete.

deleted.description: IDs of the redirections that were deleted.

notFound.description: IDs that did not match an active redirection.

index.description: The zero-based position of the item in the request payload.

reason.description: The reason the item was skipped (only set on skipped items).

UrlRedirectionSaveResult.description: Per-item outcome of a multi-item URL redirection save.

previousSigningSecret.description: The previous secret, still signed-with for 24 hours after a roll so receivers can migrate.

retriesEnabled.description: Whether failed deliveries are retried.  Defaults off.

retryCount.description: Max retries after the initial delivery attempt (1-8).

retrySpeed.description: Retry backoff base: "fast" (30s), "standard" (5m), "slow" (30m).  Exponential with jitter, capped at 24h.

secretRolledUtc.description: When the signing secret was last rolled.

secureDeliveryEnabled.description:
Opt-in for Standard Webhooks signed delivery.  Defaults false, and an absent Table column
reads false - so every webhook that existed before this feature shipped keeps its exact
legacy behavior (unsigned) until someone turns this on.  A signing secret is minted on the
first save with this enabled.

signingSecret.description:
Standard Webhooks signing secret ("whsec_" + base64).  Server-generated only - values sent by
clients are ignored on save.  Masked on reads unless the caller has Manage permission.

signingSecretJustCreated.description:
TRANSPORT ONLY - true on a save response when THAT save minted the signing secret, so a client
can present the new secret at the moment it was created.  [IgnoreProperty] keeps it out of Table
Storage; it describes one request, not the webhook.  Server-set: inbound values are ignored.

WebhookHistory.description:
One webhook delivery record from the WebHookHistory table.
PartitionKey = "{instanceGuid}.{yyyy-MM-dd}" (UTC date the event was queued), RowKey = delivery guid
(which is also the webhook-id header value sent to the receiver).
Written by the classic producer (queued) and the WebhookProcessing function (delivery results) -
this API only reads it.

attemptCount.description: Number of delivery attempts made (1 = the initial attempt).

eventKey.description: Idempotency key of the underlying content event.

httpResponseCode.description: HTTP status of the last attempt; 0 when the request itself failed (timeout, connection error).

lastAttemptDate.description: When the last delivery attempt started.

lastError.description: Short description of the last failure.

nextAttemptUtc.description: When the next retry is due, if one is scheduled.

payload.description: The JSON body that was POSTed to the webhook URL.

responseText.description: Response body from the receiver, truncated to 8KB by the delivery function.

sendDate.description: Set only when a delivery attempt succeeded (2xx).

signatureKeyCount.description:
Signatures sent in the webhook-signature header on the last attempt: 0 unsigned, 1 normally,
2 during the 24h grace window after a secret roll.

signed.description:
Whether the last attempt was sent with Standard Webhooks signature headers, as recorded by the
delivery function at send time.  Null means no record - the delivery has not been attempted yet,
or the row predates the column.  Deliberately NOT derived from the webhook's current
SecureDeliveryEnabled: that setting can be changed at any time, and re-deriving it would relabel
past deliveries with today's configuration.

webhookRowKey.description: RowKey of the webhook definition this delivery belongs to.  Null on rows that predate the feature.

isTeamUser.description: Whether this user is part of a team or not.  This value is saved in the Website DB

platformExtensions.description:
The platform integrations that are enabled for this website.
These are NOT populated by the get user call.

teamID.description: Which team the user has been authorized with.  This value is resolved at runtime.

WorkflowOperationType.description:
Workflow operation types specifically for batch processing.
Subset of BatchOperationType containing only workflow-related operations.

post.summary:
API method to create a batch from an explicit list of items and queue it.
            
Replaces Classic's `Batch/Update`, the only route that accepted an arbitrary `Items[]` and
which was not reachable from this API — every other batch endpoint here either acts on an
existing batch by id or builds the item list itself. Pair it with the `cascade-items`
endpoints on pages and content items to submit a user-pruned selection.
            
An item list longer than one batch holds is split across several rather than rejected, so
the caller does not have to page it themselves; every batchID comes back in the result.
            
As with every batch endpoint, this only enqueues: Classic enforces the caller's
permission on each item when it processes the batch, so an item the caller cannot act on
fails within the batch while the rest proceed.

post.summary:
Creates and/or updates up to 250 URL redirections in a single operation.
Items without a urlRedirectionID are created; items with one are updated (full replace).
Items that fail validation or collide with an existing origin URL are skipped and
reported in the response rather than failing the batch.

get.summary:
Exports all active URL redirections as an Excel (.xlsx) file in the same column
format the import accepts, so an export can be edited and re-imported.

post.summary:
Imports URL redirections from an Excel (.xlsx) file (up to 5000 rows). The columns
match the classic import/export: OriginURL and DestinationURL are required; HTTPCode
(defaults to 301), OriginLangCodes (semicolon-separated locale codes),
DestinationLangCode, Content and UrlRedirectionID are optional. Rows with a
UrlRedirectionID update the existing redirection, so an export can be edited and
re-imported as a bulk update. Rows that fail are skipped and reported; the Index on
each result is the row number in the file (the header is row 1).

7 days and may span at most 366; the cap is a sanity bound on the input, not a cost control -

post.summary:
API method to publish a content item together with its one-level nested content — the
non-shared, non-dynamic-page-list containers its `Content` fields point at (PROD-2489).
            
A separate route rather than a flag on `item/{contentID}/publish` because the expansion can
exceed one batch. Rather than refusing an oversized cascade, the work is split across
several batches and every batchID is returned — the shape `ImportUrlRedirections` uses
beside `SaveUrlRedirections`. `item/{contentID}/publish` is unchanged.
            
As with every batch endpoint, this only enqueues: Classic enforces the caller's permission
on each item when it processes the batch, so an item the caller cannot publish fails within
its batch while the rest proceed.

post.summary:
API method to publish a page together with its modules and their one-level nested content
(PROD-2489). This is the cascade Classic's `Pages/WorkflowAction` applied unconditionally;
here it is a route of its own, so `page/{id}/publish` keeps its page-only behaviour.
            
A page can carry more than one batch's worth of modules and links, so an oversized
expansion is split across several batches rather than refused, and every batchID is
returned. Classic still enforces per-item permissions when it processes each batch, so a
module the caller cannot publish fails inside its batch, not on this request.
